defects: asset-three-quarter.png, asset-profile.png, and asset-detail.png render the smoked-glass top, graphite frame, and fittings as a nearly black mass.
The tabletop edge and broad reflection from the approved image target are absent or too weak to read in the close production views.
Although the paired columns, under-glass rail, and T-feet exist, their component and material hierarchy is obscured.
The actual room-scale render keeps the desk silhouette but leaves it competing with the dark monitor/chair cluster; it is not a visible improvement over desk-v007.
hard_fail_reasons: The actual Godot Compatibility production captures fail the dominant material-response requirement: the glass edge/reflection and separation among glass, graphite, satin fittings, and rubber do not read clearly.
The v061 three-quarter, profile, and detail captures remain substantially darker and less differentiated than the matched desk-v007 production captures, so v007 remains the incumbent.
incumbent_comparison: v061 preserves the multipart v059/v060 geometry and validates at exact 66 x 30 x 30-inch bounds. In matched production views, however, its top and support frame collapse toward black, while v007 retains a more legible top plane and brighter glass/material highlights. The override log confirms 22 meshes were processed, but the production pixels do not show the intended hierarchy. v007 remains the incumbent.
likely_causes: Both GLTF material-factor trials and the candidate-local native StandardMaterial3D override trial fail under the same Compatibility production path, so copying nominal property values has not reproduced v007's effective visual response.

The present evidence does not isolate whether the remaining difference comes from effective per-surface material assignment, renderer/environment response, or their interaction; the actual close PNGs establish the failure but not a single engine-level cause.
The dark desk value also competes with the separate black monitors and chair in the room-scale view, reducing visible separation at the intended gameplay distance.
next_action_hypothesis: Stop desk-specific material parameter variants and keep desk-v007. If this desk returns to active work, first run a controlled material/render diagnosis with v007 and v061 under identical camera, lights, renderer, and verified per-surface effective material values; resume challenger production only after that comparison identifies a correctable stage. Do not change RoomDefinition or create another generic desk shader variant.

observations.art_direction_fit: The restrained contemporary workstation palette fits the Human Room, but the near-black production response makes this candidate a poor visual endpoint.
observations.close_up_quality: asset-three-quarter.png, asset-profile.png, and asset-detail.png show the broad glass top, supports, rail, and feet but bury their edges and fittings in darkness.
observations.gameplay_readability: room-scale.png retains the standing-desk silhouette and exact scene placement, yet the desk blends with the monitor/chair cluster more than v007 and the approved target.
observations.geometric_detail: The mesh retains the two-stage posts, under-glass rail, mounting structures, separate fittings, and T-feet; technical validation reports 22 meshes and 8,712 triangles.
observations.material_realism: The dominant glass and graphite surfaces render nearly black; the broad reflection, bright continuous edge, and distinct satin/rubber responses from the visual target are not present.
observations.proportion: Godot reports the exact 66 x 30 x 30-inch bounds, with the floor datum at zero and no RoomDefinition change.
observations.scale_fidelity: The candidate validates at the exact VisualBrief/RoomDefinition dimensions and retains the same 0.5-inch citizen context; this confirms the envelope, not visual material quality.
observations.semantic_recognizability: The asset-three-quarter and room-scale views still read as a standing computer desk from its broad plane, paired columns, and feet.
observations.silhouette_quality: The wide thin top, open knee space, paired columns, and perpendicular T-feet remain in the correct major arrangement.
observations.source_resemblance: The main standing-desk silhouette is preserved, but the photo's readable smoked-glass plane and reflective edge character are missing.
observations.surface_variation: Glass, frame, fittings, and rubber merge into a nearly uniform dark mass in the close views rather than separating into controlled materials.
observations.technical_integration: Godot 4.7.2 Compatibility imports and renders the candidate through the normal RoomScale path. Validation passes at 22 meshes, 22 surfaces, 8,712 triangles, exact bounds, and no reported issues; the visual material gate still fails.

close_inspection.evidence: The three-quarter, profile, and detail captures show major supports but leave the glass edge and attached fittings difficult to inspect because most materials collapse toward black.

edge_treatment.evidence: asset-profile.png retains a thin continuous panel, but its edge is almost black and not visibly finished to the target's glass edge response.

hardware.evidence: Mounts and fittings are present in the model but merge into the dark tabletop/frame in asset-detail.png.

joins.evidence: The support geometry is connected, but the post-to-rail and mount joins are not clearly legible against the near-black surfaces.

manufacturing_detail.evidence: The close view does not communicate the separate manufactured glass, coated frame, satin fitting, and rubber components.

material_response.evidence: The glass and coated metal are substantially darker than the approved target and desk-v007's matched production capture.

surface_variation.evidence: The tabletop and supporting components visually merge rather than show restrained but distinct material response.

thickness.evidence: The profile retains a thin continuous glass slab with no large thickness or silhouette defect.

neutral_viewer_realism.evidence: The close production images do not read as a finished smoked-glass workstation because the main materials and edge treatment are nearly black.

photo_character.evidence: Although the top and standing frame silhouette match the photograph, the glass's visible edge and broad reflective character do not survive in the actual Godot captures.
